title: Editing bioelectric pattern set points can reprogram anatomy without genome editing

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Editing bioelectric pattern set points can reprogram anatomy without genome editing

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A better strategy for regenerative medicine than genetic rewiring of cells may be to edit the pattern-homeostatic set point and let wild-type cells build to it, as shown by altering bioelectric state in planaria to give permanently double-headed worms without genomic editing.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I have previously suggested that a better strategy than cellular re-wiring at the genetic level may be to edit the pattern-homeostatic set point and let wild-type cells build to the new spec. For example, the ability to re-write target morphology in planarian regeneration was recently shown, by altering the bioelectric state in flatworms, without genomic editing, giving rise to permanently double-headed worms (Durant et al., 2017; Levin et al., 2018).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Discussion”. Scope: Regenerative medicine; planarian regeneration as the demonstrating case

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-25: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public planarian resources can examine genomic stability and molecular correlates, while published outcomes address persistent morphology. They only partly resolve whether a set point was edited and do not establish that this is a better general medical strategy.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track head-number outcomes over repeated regeneration after transient bioelectric perturbation, confirm absence of sequence edits, and compare persistence with conventional genetic interventions and alternative injury-memory mechanisms.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public molecular datasets may not link individual worms across regeneration rounds.

The regenerative-medicine superiority claim requires comparative interventions.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Permanent anatomy across asexual generations, with the genome left unchanged, is a concrete test of the planarian example. Those worm-level outcomes and sequences were published, if at all, inside the papers, and no repository lets a third party recount heads or call variants. The regenerative-medicine recommendation is broader than that example. The demonstrating case is partly documented and not reanalyzable; the strategy claim needs data the example does not supply.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: After a transient bioelectric perturbation in planaria, score head number across subsequent regeneration rounds in the absence of further treatment, and sequence the lines for coding changes. Permanent two-headed anatomy with no relevant sequence change would support set-point editing; reversion, or a fixed mutation, would refute the demonstrating case.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Phenotype counts and any sequencing of the stable lines are not in a public archive.

Planarian reference genomes do not contain the edited lines.

A planarian result does not show that the strategy works as regenerative medicine in vertebrates.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.38
data adequacy: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.55
data existence: 0.4
